[ASSISTANT_SAID] Swimming is an excellent way to improve cardiovascular endurance while being easy on the joints.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended warm-up for swimming: Easy swimming with a mix of freestyle, backstroke, and breaststroke; dynamic stretching, such as arm circles and leg kicks.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested endurance sets: Swim 4-6 sets of 200-400 meters at a moderate pace (60-70% effort) with 20-30 seconds rest between sets.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested interval training: Swim 25-50 meters at high intensity (80-90% effort) with 15-25 seconds rest, repeat for 8-12 reps.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested pyramid workout: Swim 25 meters at a moderate pace, increase distance by 25 meters each set, then decrease distance by 25 meters after reaching the peak, with 20-30 seconds rest between sets.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested sprint intervals with kicking: Swim 25 meters at high intensity (80-90% effort) with a kickboard, rest for 15-25 seconds, repeat for 8-12 reps.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested long, steady-state swim: Swim at a moderate pace (60-70% effort) for 10-20 minutes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended cool-down for swimming: Easy swimming with a mix of freestyle, backstroke, and breaststroke; static stretching, such as hamstring and shoulder stretches.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips to improve endurance: Incorporate strength training, drills, mix up strokes, gradually increase distance and intensity, and make it fun.
